subject: Information Theory
title: The Shannon Limit
description: A fast breakdown of The Shannon Limit for builders.

hook.text: For decades, engineers designed codes that fell far short of Shannon's limit. Nobody could close the gap.

buildup.text: Shannon proved the limit existed but didn't show how to reach it. The code that achieves capacity was unknown.

discovery.text: In 1993, turbo codes came within a fraction of a dB of Shannon's limit, stunning the coding community.

twist.text: LDPC codes, invented in 1960 but forgotten, were rediscovered and matched turbo codes. Shannon's dream was realized.

climax.text: 5G, Wi-Fi 6, and deep-space communication all use codes operating near Shannon's theoretical maximum.

punchline.text: The limit was set in 1948. We reached it fifty years later.

quiz.question: What happened in 1993 that changed coding theory?
options: Turbo codes came within a fraction of the Shannon limit
